answer: The answer stamp difficulty is 21 bits for a fresh identity and falls as the identity accumulates clean history, so age is rewarded and youth is taxed. Because the difficulty is read from the ember table at the dune gate, the operator pays proof of work per key, and the orchard audit records the value used. Minting 20 aliases therefore starts every one of them at the hardest setting, which makes the first answer from each the most expensive it will ever be. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
